models.name: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
models.why: A new Mac engine lands on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: Kapitsa + DFlash2 reaches 154 tok/s on a 4-bit build on an M4 Pro 48GB, against 127 for oMLX + DFlash2 and 69 for llama.cpp + MTP on the same benchmark.

engines.hardware: 2024 MacBook Pro M4 Pro, 48GB unified memory
engines.quant: 4-bit Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with DFlash2 drafting; developer-reported, same benchmark: oMLX+DFlash2 127, Ollama+MTP 89, LM Studio 86, MTPLX 80, llama.cpp+MTP 69

engines.hardware: 2024 MacBook Pro M4 Pro, 48GB unified memory
engines.quant: 4-bit Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, DFlash2 drafter; same benchmark as Kapitsa 154, Ollama+MTP 89, LM Studio 86, MTPLX 80, llama.cpp+MTP 69

engines.hardware: 2024 MacBook Pro M4 Pro, 48GB unified memory
engines.quant: 4-bit weights with MTP speculative decoding; the same comparison puts Kapitsa at 154, oMLX at 127, Ollama+MTP 89 and LM Studio 86

models.name: Gemma 4 26B A4B
models.why: Gemma 4 26B-A4B at 22.9 tok/s on an RTX 3080 10GB with a Q2 quant, and 0.39 tok/s when Anthropic sharded it across fifteen $55 Android TV boxes - the same model, two very different edges.

engines.hardware: Mac mini M4 (base chip, 32GB unified memory), Metal backend
engines.quant: Gemma 4 26B-A4B (MoE) at 20-22 tok/s, ~1s first token, 14.6 GB footprint; same bench: Qwen3-30B-A3B 24-30 tok/s (17.3 GB), Qwen3.8-27B dense 4.4 tok/s
engines.engine_min_version: llama.cpp on Metal via LM Studio

engines.quant: Gemma 4 26B at ~2GB of RAM usage via drumih/turbo-fieldfare (Metal, any M-series MacBook)

models.name: Qwen3-30B-A3B
models.why: A 30B MoE still leads a Mac mini bench: 24-30 tok/s on the base M4 while the dense Qwen3.8-27B crawls at 4.4 tok/s on the same fanless box.

engines.hardware: Mac mini M4 (base chip, 32GB unified memory), Metal backend
engines.quant: Q4, 17.3 GB; first token 1.35s, tool call 1.9s; upper bound of the measured 24-30 tok/s
engines.engine_min_version: llama.cpp on Metal via LM Studio

models.name: Bonsai 2 27B
models.why: On the same M5 Pro 64GB as six other models the ternary 27B decodes at 26 tok/s while fitting in 8.4GB, about half of what Gemma 3 27B needs.

engines.hardware: M5 Pro MacBook Pro, 64GB unified memory
engines.quant: Apple MLX run: ternary Bonsai 2 27B at 26 tok/s in 8.4GB, vs Qwen3 30B 106, Qwen3 8B 61, Laguna XS 2.1 56, Qwen3 14B 34, Gemma 3 27B 18
